figures.finding: The Maldives has no rule of its own for child performers: no minor under sixteen may be employed save in training tied to education or in the family's own line of work, any minor (under eighteen) needs the guardian's written approval, may not be kept at work in school hours or after 11 pm, and must be entered in the employer's register of minors.

sources.said: Minors under the age of sixteen years shall not be employed except in connection with training associated with their education or deportment.

A minor shall only be engaged in any employment or work, in accordance with Section 6 and Section 7, after the written approval of the minor's legal guardian or guardian recognised at law has been obtained.
A minor employed in accordance with Section 6, shall not be required to be at work during school hours of the minor. b) A minor shall not be required to work after 11pm at night
A child shall be deemed to be under eighteen years of age as provided for in Law No 9/91

figures.finding: A company director must be at least eighteen, and directors must be shareholders.
figures.applies: Maldives, Companies Act 10/96 s. 45(c), as WIPO Lex holds it; whether a later companies act replaced it was not checked.

sources.said: A director of a company shall be at least 18 years of age.
